title: Seat liveness leaf: a silence-vs-absolute-cap decider and a Windows process-tree/CPU probe, where an unobservable seat is never killed for silence
description:
LEAF split out of task-8f653d86bb4f445cb7ee358c5559f99a ("The seat timeout is a wall-clock cap from spawn, not a liveness test") by architect-73d103f8 on 2026-09-18, because the whole fix measured at 11 files against the 10-file cap. That row is the CONSUMER and declares dependsOn on this one; it wires what this row builds into agent-spawner.ts, adds the absolute-cap knob, the moe start env roster and the docs. THIS row lands a pure module and its tests only, and touches no existing production file.

WHY IT EXISTS (measured live on UnAI 2026-09-18, and at HEAD). agent-spawner.ts:399-402 arms `setTimeout(beginTermination, timeoutMs)` once at spawn and never rearms it, so a seat is killed at MOE_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS however busy it is. The quiet notice at :404-414 cannot help: the seat is `claude -p` WITHOUT --output-format, which writes nothing until it finishes, so every seat shows "0 bytes seen" for its whole life. Node 5 (15f56b77) was at minute 26 with a live bash.exe tool child started 60 s earlier (claude.exe cpu 25 s) and was on course to be killed at minute 30 mid-work.

WHY NOT STREAM OUTPUT INSTEAD. The parent row allows either streaming (`--output-format stream-json`) or a process probe. Streaming is REJECTED: apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/seat-exit-classifier.ts pattern-matches the seat's TEXT to detect provider limits, with regexes measured against specific claude.exe builds (`/You've hit your usage limit(?![.\w])/iu`, the 429 banner), and its own comment at :58 warns that a seat printing "rate limit" inside its JSON output must NOT park the provider. Routing everything the model says through JSON events risks a seat whose model merely writes "rate limit" in a code comment falsely pausing the whole fleet's provider. A process probe changes no output format and leaves the classifier untouched.

THE TWO LOAD-BEARING FACTS the design must honour:
1. THE SEAT ROOT IS A SHELL, NOT THE PROVIDER. On Windows the seat is spawned through cmd.exe (governor observed cmd pid 49960 -> claude.exe 17324). So "a live descendant exists", measured from the spawned pid, is ALWAYS true while the seat runs, because the provider process itself is that descendant. A tool child must be counted STRICTLY BELOW the provider process. CPU progress summed over the whole tree is the more robust signal and must be honoured independently.
2. ONLY POSITIVELY OBSERVED SILENCE MAY KILL (epic rail 4: unverifiable evidence gains no authority). A probe that fails, times out, or has no implementation for the platform reports UNKNOWN, and UNKNOWN never earns a silence kill; only the absolute cap applies then. Without this rule, silent `claude -p` seats on any platform without a probe would be killed SOONER than today.

CONTRACT this row must export (the consumer row plans against these exact names; changing them requires amending task-8f653d86):
- `SeatLivenessSample` = { kind: "OBSERVED"; cpuMs: number; toolChildren: readonly { pid: number; command: string }[] } | { kind: "UNKNOWN"; reason: string }
- `SeatProbe` = (seatPid: number) => Promise<SeatLivenessSample>
- `SeatLivenessVerdict` = { kind: "CONTINUE" } | { kind: "KILL_SILENT"; silentMs: number; lastActivity: string | null } | { kind: "KILL_ABSOLUTE_CAP"; ageMs: number; lastActivity: string | null }
- `createSeatLivenessTracker({ startedAtMs, silenceMs, maxRuntimeMs })` returning { noteOutput(nowMs), noteSample(nowMs, sample), verdict(nowMs) } — ALL liveness state lives here so the 480-line spawner stays thin.
- `createWindowsSeatProbe(run?: RuntimeCommand)` — one Get-CimInstance Win32_Process query per call behind an injectable runner, following apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/runtime-broker-identity.ts:14/:38 (the `RuntimeCommand` seam and `runPowerShell`).

OUT OF SCOPE: agent-spawner.ts, the knobs, the env roster, the docs (task-8f653d86 owns them); a POSIX probe (follow-up — on a platform with no probe a stuck seat now lives until the absolute cap instead of 30 min, which is the deliberate cost of never killing a seat on unverifiable evidence).
definitionOfDone: apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/seat-liveness.ts exports the exact contract named in the description (SeatLivenessSample, SeatProbe, SeatLivenessVerdict, createSeatLivenessTracker, createWindowsSeatProbe) with its one-line .js bridge beside it, and the file stays at or under 250 lines.

The tracker never returns KILL_SILENT unless silence was POSITIVELY observed: an arm feeds only UNKNOWN samples past the silence window and asserts verdict kind CONTINUE, then past the absolute cap asserts KILL_ABSOLUTE_CAP; a second arm feeds OBSERVED samples with no CPU progress, no tool child and no output past the window and asserts KILL_SILENT with the exact silentMs. Reason codes asserted by value, never merely 'not CONTINUE'.

Each liveness signal is honoured INDEPENDENTLY, one arm per signal: output alone, a tool child alone (CPU flat), and CPU progress alone (no tool child) each keep the verdict CONTINUE past the silence window. The tool-child arm uses a tree where the only descendants are the shell and the provider process and asserts that does NOT count as a tool child.

The Windows probe is driven through its injectable runner in tests (no real process needed): a well-formed CIM answer yields OBSERVED with the summed CPU and the tool children below the provider; a failing, empty, malformed or timed-out runner yields UNKNOWN with a named reason, never OBSERVED and never a throw. One real-host arm, gated like apps/daemon/src/deployment/migrate-down-real.test.ts, probes the test runner's own pid on Windows and asserts OBSERVED.

Gate quoted with its `Test Files N passed` count line: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/orchestrator/seat-liveness.test.ts`, plus `pnpm typecheck` (the daemon project now carries erasableSyntaxOnly, so the new module must be erasable).

implementationPlan.description: MEASURE, and calibrate the one number the design cannot guess. (a) Confirm the CPU units against a live process: run `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "ProcessId=<pid>" -Property KernelModeTime,UserModeTime` twice a known interval apart on a busy process, and confirm `(KernelModeTime+UserModeTime)/10_000` tracks milliseconds of CPU; planningNotes measured 937500+2656250 ticks = 359 ms on a pwsh. (b) CALIBRATE THE CPU-PROGRESS THRESHOLD: start a provider process that is ALIVE BUT IDLE — a `node -e "setInterval(()=>{},1000)"` stands in for claude.exe waiting on the model API — sample its CPU across several 60-second intervals, and record the per-interval delta. Then do the same for a process doing real work. Choose the named constant comfortably ABOVE the idle delta and far below the busy one, and record both measured numbers in the step note and in a comment beside the constant. That constant is what separates 'waiting' from 'working'. (c) Measure a real seat-shaped tree: spawn a long-lived child through `cmd.exe` the way agent-spawner.ts does with `shell: true`, give it its own child, and dump the tree with one CIM query — confirm the spawned pid is cmd.exe, its direct child is the stand-in provider, and the grandchild is what a tool child looks like. Record the tree.
implementationPlan.note:
MEASURED 2026-09-18 12:15-12:28Z. Pure measurement: no repo writes. The scripts are out of tree at %TEMP%/moe-task-eca3780d-worker-e0435164/{measure,hung}.mjs. Each sample is ONE cold powershell.exe Get-CimInstance Win32_Process query, costing 360-582 ms over 676-739 processes.

(a) CPU UNITS CONFIRMED. I compared CIM (KernelModeTime+UserModeTime)/10_000 with the stand-in's own process.cpuUsage() (user+system)/1000, taken within 1 s of each other: 12125 vs 12124, 23984.4 vs 23983, 241281.25 vs 241265, 125 vs 124, 140.6 vs 140. The CIM values are multiples of 15.625 ms (one Windows clock tick), so a threshold must sit many ticks above that quantum.

(b) CALIBRATION, in ms of CPU per 60 s interval:
- idle node `setInterval(()=>{},1000)`: 0-31.3
- node provider plus a bash->sleep tool child: 15.6-31.3
- HUNG REAL `claude -p` (claude.exe against a localhost fake API that accepted POST /v1/messages and never answered): 156.3, 328.1, 109.4, 171.9
- REAL WORKING moe-next seat cmd.exe#744 > claude.exe#52460 (`claude -p --setting-sources "" ... --strict-mcp-config`), with no tool child at the sample instants: 765.6, 859.4, 781.3, 1578.1
- busy node at 10% duty: 5859-6000; at 100%: about 59600
Chosen constant: CPU_PROGRESS_MS_PER_MINUTE = 500. It is a RATE (cpuDelta scaled by elapsed wall time), not a per-sample delta. The consumer's cadence is DEFAULT_QUIET_NOTICE_MS 60_000 and injectable, so a per-sample delta would move with it. 500 is roughly the geometric midpoint of the hung max (328) and the working min (766): 1.5x above hung, 0.65x of working, 16x above idle node. If it is too low, a hung seat looks alive and dies only at the absolute cap (the safe direction). If it is too high, a working seat with no tool child and under 500/min for a whole 30-minute silence window is killed; one model call lasts minutes.
Finding against off-board f1fd5f6d: its CPU_ACTIVITY_FLOOR_MS = 250 per 60 s tick is exceeded by a HUNG claude.exe (328), so a hung seat's silence clock resets. Its comment's premise ("idle Node ... single-digit ms per minute") holds for node, not for claude.exe.

(c) SEAT TREE. From a node parent with windowsHide, spawn(line,[],{shell:true}) gives cmd.exe with TWO direct children, conhost.exe AND the provider node.exe; below it, bash.exe > sleep.exe. The real wrapper seat has a console, so it has no conhost: cmd.exe#744 > claude.exe#52460.
HAZARD MEASURED: the plan's "the root's direct child" is ambiguous. My first script took the first depth-1 node, which was conhost.exe, and read the provider's CPU as a constant 15.625. So the probe must pick the provider as the root's direct child that is NOT conhost.exe, and never count conhost.exe as a tool child.
Also seen: an interactive claude.exe#7024 carries persistent helper children (node.exe MCP, serena.exe>python>cmd>node). Its tree CPU went NEGATIVE (-31594 and -26547 per minute) as children exited, so the CPU baseline must rebase to the latest sample.

COLLISION, still open: off-board f1fd5f6d (branch fix/seat-liveness-silence-kill, not on origin/main c09fcc06) creates the SAME path seat-liveness.ts with a different contract. I asked the governor in msg-3ac96695; there was no reply at step close.

Peer dirt: 10 .moe and 10 product paths, not mine and untouched.

implementationPlan.description: RED — the tracker, pure and clock-injected, in a NEW apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/seat-liveness.test.ts. Every arm asserts the verdict BY VALUE, including `silentMs` / `ageMs` and `lastActivity` — never merely 'not CONTINUE'. DoD 2: (1) only UNKNOWN samples, fed past the silence window — verdict CONTINUE; then past the absolute cap — KILL_ABSOLUTE_CAP with the exact ageMs. This is THE arm that proves an unobservable seat is never killed for silence. (2) OBSERVED samples with no tool child, flat CPU and no output, past the window — KILL_SILENT with the exact silentMs. DoD 3, one arm per signal, each keeping CONTINUE past the window on its own: (3) `noteOutput` alone; (4) a tool child alone with CPU flat; (5) CPU progress alone with no tool child. Plus the edges the silence rule in planningNotes exists for: (6) a single UNKNOWN mid-silence DELAYS the kill by exactly one window rather than blocking it forever — assert CONTINUE just before `lastUnknownAtMs + silenceMs` and KILL_SILENT just after; (7) the FIRST OBSERVED sample never counts as CPU progress; (8) the absolute cap wins even when the seat is busy at that moment; (9) a CPU delta just BELOW the calibrated threshold is not progress and one just above is — so the constant from step 1 is pinned by value. Run the file and CONFIRM RED before step 3; quote the failures.

GREEN — the tracker. Create apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/seat-liveness.ts exporting the contract pinned in the row description: `SeatLivenessSample`, `SeatProbe`, `SeatLivenessVerdict`, and `createSeatLivenessTracker({ startedAtMs, silenceMs, maxRuntimeMs })` returning `{ noteOutput, noteSample, verdict }`. Implement the silence rule EXACTLY as written in planningNotes.designDecisions — absolute cap checked first; KILL_SILENT only when inactivity has lasted the window AND no UNKNOWN fell within the last window AND an OBSERVED sample landed after both the last activity and the last UNKNOWN. Write that three-clause rule as a comment at the site, with one line on why clause (b) exists: an unobservable window is not evidence of silence, and without it a silent `claude -p` seat on a platform with no probe would be killed sooner than today. Declare the calibrated CPU threshold from step 1 as a named constant carrying both measured numbers. Create the one-line bridge apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/seat-liveness.js containing exactly `export * from "./seat-liveness.ts";`. The daemon project now carries `erasableSyntaxOnly`, so no parameter properties, enums or namespaces. Confirm every arm from step 2 is GREEN.

The Windows probe (DoD 4), RED then GREEN, driven entirely through an injected runner so no real process is needed. (a) In apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/runtime-broker-identity.ts add `export` to `runPowerShell` and to `powershell` — nothing else changes; reusing them keeps ONE process runner with ONE env scrub and ONE timeout rather than two copies free to drift. (b) Add `createWindowsSeatProbe(run: RuntimeCommand = runPowerShell, platform = process.platform)` to seat-liveness.ts: one `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Property ProcessId,ParentProcessId,Name,CommandLine,KernelModeTime,UserModeTime` per call, emitted in a line format you can parse without ambiguity. Walk the tree from the seat pid; identify the provider (the root's direct child when the root is cmd.exe, else the root); report tool children as descendants STRICTLY BELOW the provider with their command lines; sum CPU over the whole tree as `(KernelModeTime + UserModeTime) / 10_000`. (c) Tests in seat-liveness.test.ts, each asserting by value: a well-formed snapshot of shell -> provider -> tool yields OBSERVED with the exact summed cpuMs and exactly one tool child; a snapshot of ONLY shell -> provider yields OBSERVED with ZERO tool children — the arm that stops every seat looking busy forever; known tick values yield the exact millisecond total, pinning the 10_000 divisor; and every failure yields UNKNOWN with its own named reason and never a throw — a runner that rejects, one that returns empty output, one that returns unparseable output, a snapshot that does not contain the seat pid, and `platform: "linux"`. A probe that turns a failure into OBSERVED is the one bug that would let the tracker kill on non-evidence, so each failure arm is load-bearing.

The real-host arm and the mutation drill. (A) Add ONE real-host arm in seat-liveness.test.ts gated exactly like apps/daemon/src/deployment/migrate-down-real.test.ts:54 — `const RUN = process.env.MOE_SEAT_PROBE_REAL === "1"` with `it.runIf(RUN)` — that runs the REAL `createWindowsSeatProbe()` against the test runner's own `process.pid` on Windows and asserts OBSERVED with a positive cpuMs. Run it WITH the flag and quote the count line showing it EXECUTED — an `it.runIf(false)` arm exits 0 with nothing run, so a bare exit 0 proves nothing — then once WITHOUT the flag to show the gate actually controls it. (B) MUTATION DRILL on the correctness core: make the tracker treat an UNKNOWN sample as silence, and confirm step 2's arm (1) goes RED; separately make the probe count the provider process itself as a tool child, and confirm the shell->provider-only arm goes RED. Quote each failing line. seat-liveness.ts is NEW, so `git diff` cannot see it and is NOT a valid restore proof (global rail 13): back the file up out of tree to `%TEMP%/moe-task-eca3780d-seat-liveness-<workerId>.ts` recording its SHA256 (task id in the path, because seat ids are reused and a seat-only backup can hold the wrong vintage), restore by copying the backup back, and prove the restore by SHA256 equality in a call SEPARATE from the restore. Record both hashes.

GATES AND ADVERSARIAL REVIEW. (A) `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/orchestrator/seat-liveness.test.ts src/orchestrator/runtime-broker-identity.test.ts` with its `Test Files N passed` line quoted — read the OUTPUT, not the exit code. runtime-broker-identity.test.ts is in the gate because step 4 edited its module. (B) `pnpm typecheck`, projects counted; the daemon project carries `erasableSyntaxOnly`, so this is what proves the new module is erasable. (C) `wc -l apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/seat-liveness.ts` at or under 250 (DoD 1); if it is over, split the probe into its own module rather than trim comments. (D) ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, recorded in the completion record: Can any sequence of samples produce KILL_SILENT without a positively observed silent window — walk UNKNOWN-then-OBSERVED, OBSERVED-then-UNKNOWN, and a probe that stops being called. Can a busy seat ever be killed for silence — a seat mid tool call, a seat waiting on a long model call, a seat whose provider has a persistent helper child? Does a CPU counter that goes BACKWARDS (a child exits, so the summed total drops) read as progress or as anything harmful? What does a probe answer when the seat pid is reused by an unrelated process after the seat exits? Is the calibrated threshold defensible from the step-1 numbers, and what does a seat look like if it is wrong in each direction? (E) State in the completion record the one deliberate relaxation of the row description: `runPowerShell` and `powershell` in runtime-broker-identity.ts gained `export`, and why reuse beat duplication. Record as a follow-up comment, not a new row: a POSIX probe, so a stuck seat there is killed for silence rather than only at the absolute cap.

reopenReason:
UNBLOCKED AND RE-SCOPED by governor ruling, answering the worker's (a)/(b) question. The answer is (a) WITH A CORRECTION, not a retirement. Measured: origin/main 31b8191b contains 4eb87ec4, the same delivery as the off-board branch, shipping seat-liveness-probe.ts, MOE_AGENT_SILENCE_MS and the silence-based kill. So the parent row task-8f653d86 is ARCHIVED as delivered and this row must NOT build a second liveness implementation — DoD 1's createSeatLivenessTracker/SeatProbe/verdict contract is withdrawn, because building it now would be an add/add duplicate of the landed createSeatLiveness.

What this row becomes, per the owner's direction that a bug in Moe gets fixed at source: a CORRECTION against the LANDED code, carrying exactly the two defects this row's own measurement found and nothing else.
1. AN UNOBSERVABLE SEAT MUST NOT BE KILLED FOR SILENCE. The landed design treats an unobserved process tree as silence ("FAIL-CLOSED"), which inverts this row's rule 2. A probe that cannot see the tree knows nothing; killing on that is killing on ignorance.
2. THE CPU FLOOR DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE. The landed floor of 250 ms/tick sits INSIDE the measured hung-seat band: a hung claude.exe measured 109-328 ms/min against a working seat's 766-1578 ms/min. A floor that a hung seat can cross cannot separate hung from working. Re-measure both bands on this host, then set the floor from the measurement and say in the code what it was calibrated against.

ARCHITECT: re-plan from scratch against the landed implementation. Read seat-liveness-probe.ts and agent-spawner.ts at origin/main FIRST; the old plan's file and contract no longer exist as planned. Keep the row small — this is two named corrections, not a rewrite. The worker was right to stop and ask rather than build a duplicate, and the 25-minute silence on msg-3ac96695 / msg-202cfe9e was my delay, not theirs.

2. COLLISION. DoD 1 creates apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/seat-liveness.ts with createSeatLivenessTracker/SeatProbe/noteSample/verdict. The branch creates the same path with createSeatLiveness/tick/formatDuration/CPU_ACTIVITY_FLOOR_MS, and its agent-spawner.ts imports `{ createSeatLiveness, formatDuration } from "./seat-liveness.js"`. Landing both is an add/add conflict. Under the landing recipe `merge-tree -X ours <branch> origin/main` the branch side wins silently, so either main's spawner import breaks or the row's consumer does. The delivered bytes would not work. That is a hard-block condition under the delivery-bias rail. Building it under another name instead would ship a second, competing liveness implementation, which is the duplicate the stale-description rail forbids.

3. DESIGN DIVERGENCE, which matters whichever way this is ruled. c3ae1ffa's settle() treats an unobserved tree as silence ("FAIL-CLOSED: an unobserved tree grants no liveness"). A probe that fails or is absent never refreshes lastActivityAt, so a `claude -p` seat, which prints nothing, is killed at 20 min whenever the probe cannot see it. That is sooner than the old 30 min cap. This row's rule 2 says the opposite: UNKNOWN never earns a silence kill.

4. CALIBRATION, from step 1 (full numbers in the step-1 note). In ms of CPU per 60 s:
- a HUNG real `claude -p` (claude.exe against a localhost API that accepted POST /v1/messages and never answered): 156, 328, 109, 172
- a WORKING moe-next seat cmd.exe#744 > claude.exe#52460 with no tool child: 766, 859, 781, 1578
- an idle node: 0-31
c3ae1ffa's CPU_ACTIVITY_FLOOR_MS = 250 per tick is flagged in its own comment as "UNMEASURED". A hung claude.exe crosses it (328), and each crossing resets the silence clock, so the silence kill rarely fires for exactly the hang it targets. The seat then falls through to the 2 h cap. A rate threshold of about 500 ms/min separates the two measured populations: it is roughly the geometric midpoint of 328 and 766.

5. conhost.exe HAZARD. When the spawner has no console, the seat's cmd.exe has TWO direct children: conhost.exe and the provider. The live wrapper seat had none. A rule of the form "the provider is the root's direct child" must skip conhost.exe; my first measurement did not, and read the provider's CPU as a constant 15.625 ms. c3ae1ffa counts descendants above the minimum seen, which absorbs a steady conhost.

comments.author: governor-cc0cc843
comments.content:
GOVERNOR: measurements to carry into the re-plan, so nobody re-derives them. All from worker-e0435164 (msg-3ac96695, msg-202cfe9e, step-1 note), taken against the LANDED design that reached main as 4eb87ec4.

1. A HUNG SEAT IS NOT CPU-IDLE. A real claude.exe pointed at a localhost fake API that accepted POST /v1/messages and never answered accrued 156, 328, 109 and 172 ms of CPU per 60 s. The landed CPU_ACTIVITY_FLOOR_MS is 250 per tick, justified as "idle Node ... single-digit ms per minute". The hung seat crosses 250 in some minutes, and每 crossing resets the silence clock, so a hung seat rarely reaches 20 consecutive quiet ticks — the exact hang the silence kill exists to catch. A real working seat (cmd.exe > claude.exe) measured 766-1578 ms per minute. The usable gap is only ~2.3x, so the floor must be calibrated between the bands and must say what it was calibrated against.

2. UNOBSERVED IS NOT SILENT, and today it is worse than the old behaviour. When the probe returns null, throws, or is absent, settle(sample=null) never refreshes lastActivityAt, so a `claude -p` seat that prints nothing is killed at MOE_AGENT_SILENCE_MS (default 20 min) — SOONER than the 30-minute cap it replaced. That inverts this row's rule 2.

3. conhost.exe CAN BE A DIRECT CHILD of the seat's cmd.exe, a sibling of the provider, when the spawner has no console (windowsHide from a console-less parent — the live wrapper seat had none). Any rule shaped "the provider is the root's direct child" must skip conhost.exe. The worker's first script did not, and read the provider's CPU as a constant 15.625 ms.

4. Also landed in the same commit, worth knowing before planning: MOE_AGENT_SILENCE_MS defaults to 20 min and MOE_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS's default moved from 30 min to 2 h.

Scope reminder from the ruling: this row is a CORRECTION against the landed createSeatLiveness/tick/formatDuration contract. Do not create a second seat-liveness module, and do not reintroduce the withdrawn createSeatLivenessTracker/SeatProbe contract.

Measured on this pwsh: Kernel=937500, User=2656250, i.e. 3,593,750 ticks = 359 ms. So `cpuMs = (KernelModeTime + UserModeTime) / 10_000`. A divisor wrong by 10^4 makes any CPU-progress threshold meaningless and must be pinned by a test that feeds known tick values.

(2) SNAPSHOT COST (run-observed). One full `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Property ProcessId,ParentProcessId,Name,KernelModeTime,UserModeTime` over 637 processes took ~204 ms in a warm pwsh. The probe additionally spawns a cold powershell.exe per call. Once a minute per seat that is fine; it also means a call can outlast a short interval, which is why the consumer must not stack overlapping calls.

(3) THE SEAM TO REUSE. apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/runtime-broker-identity.ts exports `RuntimeCommand` (:14, `(file, args) => Promise<string>`) and `resolveRuntimeBrokerPid` (:38), but `runPowerShell` (a const running execFile with timeout 30_000, windowsHide, and an env scrubbed to SystemRoot/WINDIR/TEMP/TMP) and `powershell()` (the System32 path) are PRIVATE. Reusing them needs a one-word `export` on each. That relaxes the leaf description's 'touches no existing production file' by exactly those two words, recorded here deliberately: duplicating a process runner that carries its own env scrubbing and timeout would leave two copies free to drift. No test pins that module's export SET — runtime-broker-identity.test.ts imports only `parseRuntimeBroker` and `resolveRuntimeBrokerPid` — and its .js bridge is `export *`, so new exports flow through. The existing precedent also fixes the platform behaviour to mirror: `resolveRuntimeBrokerPid(..., platform = process.platform)` returns null off win32 and swallows every error into null.

(4) THE ERASABLE GUARD IS LIVE. `apps/daemon/tsconfig.json:4` now carries `"erasableSyntaxOnly": true` (task-4444d180's change is in the tree), so the new module must avoid parameter properties, enums and namespaces — typecheck will refuse them.

(5) REAL-HOST GATING PRECEDENT. apps/daemon/src/deployment/migrate-down-real.test.ts:54 `const RUN = process.env.MOE_MIGRATION_RESTORE === "1";` with `it.runIf(RUN)(...)` at :128.

(6) THE CPU-NOISE PROBLEM, and why the design survives it. A claude seat spends most of its life waiting on the model API: no tool child, no output, near-zero CPU. Yet node's idle event loop still ticks some CPU. So 'any CPU increase' would make every seat look alive forever, and too high a threshold would make a waiting seat look dead. The threshold must be CALIBRATED FROM MEASUREMENT (step 1) and live as a named constant with that measurement recorded. The design is robust to mis-calibration in BOTH directions: set too low, an idle seat looks alive and falls back to the absolute cap (the safe direction); set too high, a working seat still shows a tool child during every tool call, and a single model call lasts minutes, far below the 30-minute default silence window.
